destination_research.summary: December is an excellent time to visit Dubai for Pakistani travelers interested in food, shopping, beaches and sightseeing. Expect warm, pleasant weather and lively crowds. Stay in Dubai Marina/JBR, Downtown, or Palm Jumeirah for easy access to beaches, malls and iconic landmarks. Daily expenses (excluding lodging and flights) average around $110 per person, covering meals, transport and entry fees. The city’s public‑transport network—metro, bus, tram, abra and monorail—makes getting around affordable, while taxis and rideshare apps offer convenience. Visa requirements are straightforward for Pakistani passport holders but must be met precisely.
major_attractions: Desert Safari (dune bashing, camel ride, BBQ)
Dubai Creek & Al Fahidi Historical Neighborhood
Mall of the Emirates (including Ski Dubai)
destination_research.best_time_to_visit: December (part of the November‑March window) offers pleasant temperatures (mid‑20s °C), low humidity and sunny days – ideal for beach time, outdoor sightseeing and desert activities. It is also peak tourist season, so attractions and beaches will be busy.
travel_considerations: Carry both cash (AED) and a credit/debit card; many places accept cards but small vendors may prefer cash.
Dress modestly in public areas (shoulders and knees covered) despite the liberal vibe, especially in traditional neighborhoods.
December is peak season; book popular attractions (Burj Khalifa, desert safari) in advance.
Stay hydrated and use sunscreen even in cooler weather.
Check if any major events (e.g., Dubai Shopping Festival) coincide with your dates, as they can affect crowd levels and prices.
destination_research.visa_and_entry_notes: Pakistani passport holders need a UAE tourist e‑Visa. Required documents include a valid passport (minimum 6 months), a recent passport‑size photo, the Pakistani CNIC (or equivalent ID), proof of onward travel, hotel booking, medical insurance valid in the UAE, and proof of sufficient funds (at least 3000 AED in cash or a credit card). The e‑Visa is typically valid for up to 60 days. Processing is done online through the GDRFA portal or authorized agencies. Travelers should verify the latest requirements and fees on the official UAE immigration website or through the UAE embassy before applying.
destination_research.cost_notes: Dubai is a high‑cost destination. Food ranges from $10‑$20 for a meal at a mid‑range restaurant to $30‑$60 at upscale venues. Public transport (metro, bus, water‑taxi) is cheap (≈$1‑$3 per ride), while taxis/Uber start around $3 plus $0.50 per km. Major attractions (Burj Khalifa ‘At The Top’, Atlantis Aquaventure, desert safari) cost $40‑$100 per person. These figures exclude accommodation and international flights.
